This question refers to a common superstition in some cultures, especially in East and Southeast Asia, regarding behaviors during the New Year and their supposed influence on the rest of the year. The belief is that your actions and emotions during the New Year set the tone for the coming year. Specifically, it is said that if you cry during the New Year, you may continue to cry or be sad throughout the year. 

Option A says you will cry for the rest of the year, which matches the superstition most closely. Option B says you will be sad, which is similar but less specific. Option C says you will be unlucky, which is a broader interpretation but not the usual phrasing of the superstition. Option D says nothing happens, which contradicts the superstition.

Based on the traditional superstition, the best answer is:

Answer: A
